subject: chemistry
title: Strong and weak acids
key_idea: A strong acid is completely ionised in water and a weak acid is only partially ionised. Strength is not the same as concentration. Each fall of one pH unit means ten times more hydrogen ions.

blocks.text: This section covers strength: how far an acid ionises in water. Some boards test this in the Higher tier only.

items.meaning: An acid molecule splitting up in water to release hydrogen ions, H⁺.
An acid that is completely ionised in aqueous solution.
An acid that is only partially ionised in aqueous solution.

items: Strong acids include hydrochloric, nitric and sulfuric acids.
Weak acids include ethanoic, citric and carbonic acids.
Hydrochloric acid ionises completely: HCl → H⁺ + Cl⁻.
Ethanoic acid ionises only partly, so most molecules stay as they are: CH₃COOH ⇌ H⁺ + CH₃COO⁻.

diagram.alt: A strong acid and a weak acid of the same concentration compared.
items: Strong acid
Weak acid
Strong acid: completely ionised. Weak acid: partially ionised.
At the same concentration, the stronger acid has more H⁺ ions and a lower pH.

blocks.text: Concentration describes how much acid is dissolved in a given volume. It is a different idea from strength.

items.meaning: A large amount of acid dissolved in a given volume of solution.
A small amount of acid dissolved in a given volume of solution.

items: Concentration is measured in mol/dm³, the amount of acid per unit volume.
A strong acid can be made into a concentrated solution or a dilute solution.
Dilute hydrochloric acid is both strong and dilute. It is completely ionised and has a small amount of acid per unit volume.
Adding water dilutes an acid. The concentration of hydrogen ions decreases and the pH increases.
Strength is about ionisation. Concentration is about the amount of acid per unit volume.
Diluting an acid lowers the hydrogen ion concentration and raises the pH.

blocks.text: (Whole numbers of pH only.) The pH depends on the concentration of hydrogen ions.

items: The higher the concentration of H⁺ ions, the lower the pH.
As the pH **decreases by one unit**, the hydrogen ion concentration **increases by a factor of 10**.
As the pH increases by one unit, the hydrogen ion concentration decreases by a factor of 10.
Both strength and concentration change the pH. A more concentrated or stronger acid has a lower pH.

blocks.label: Change in hydrogen ion concentration
where: change in pH: a whole number of pH units
factor: how many times the H⁺ concentration changes

diagram.alt: Move the pH to see how many times more hydrogen ions an acid has than neutral water.

outputs.label: Times more H⁺ ions than neutral water (pH 7)
pH after diluting by a factor of 10

items.text: 10 cm³ made up to 1000 cm³ is a dilution by a factor of 1000 ÷ 10 = 100.
A factor of 100 is 10 × 10, so the pH changes by 2 units.
Dilution raises the pH. From pH 2 the new pH is 2 + 2 = 4.

items: One pH unit is a factor of 10 in hydrogen ion concentration.
Two pH units is a factor of 100. Three is a factor of 1000.

checks.q: What is meant by a weak acid?
checks.a: An acid that is only partially ionised in aqueous solution.

checks.q: A solution of pH 3 is diluted until its pH is 5. By what factor has the hydrogen ion concentration decreased?
checks.a: 100. The pH has increased by 2 units, so the concentration has decreased by 10 × 10.

checks.q: Explain why a weak acid has a higher pH than a strong acid of the same concentration.
checks.a: The weak acid is only partially ionised, so it produces a lower concentration of hydrogen ions.

mistakes.wrong: A strong acid is one where the hydrogen ions are ionised.
mistakes.right: Hydrogen is ionising and H⁺ are ionised are not accepted. The acid is completely ionised (or dissociated) in aqueous solution.

mistakes.wrong: A strong acid is one with a low pH.
mistakes.right: References to pH are ignored when asked what strong means. Say the acid is completely ionised in aqueous solution.

mistakes.wrong: Ethanoic acid reacts more slowly because there are fewer acid molecules.
mistakes.right: Both solutions have the same concentration. Ethanoic acid is weak, so it is partially ionised, the concentration of hydrogen ions is lower and collisions are less frequent.

worked_example.question:
Dilute hydrochloric acid is a strong acid.

Explain why an acid can be described as both strong and dilute.
answer_points: Strong because it is completely ionised (dissociated) in aqueous solution.
Dilute because it contains a small amount of acid per unit volume.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each word. Do not mention pH in the strong part.

mistakes.wrong: A dilute acid is not concentrated.
mistakes.right: Not concentrated and weak concentration are ignored. Say dilute means a low concentration of the acid (or solute).

mistakes.wrong: A strong acid has a low pH.
mistakes.right: All references to pH are ignored. Say a strong acid is fully dissociated (ionised) to form hydrogen ions.

mistakes.wrong: When the hydrogen ion concentration decreases by a factor of 10, the pH increases.
mistakes.right: Increases alone is ignored. Say the pH increases by one.

worked_example.question:
The dilute hydrochloric acid used in this reaction is a strong acid.

Explain the meaning of the terms dilute and strong acid.
answer_points: Of the solute (acid, or hydrogen ions).
Strong acid: the acid is fully dissociated (ionised).
worked_example.tip: Two marks for each term. The second mark for dilute depends on the first. Ignore references to pH.

exam_phrases: strong acids are fully ionised or completely dissociated (in aqueous solution)
weak acids are partially ionised or not completely dissociated
a dilute solution has a low ratio of acid to volume of solution
a strong acid can be made into a concentrated or a dilute solution
concentration of H+ decreased by a factor of 100, pH increased by 2
using a higher ratio of acid to water

mistakes.wrong: Strong acids have many H⁺ ions and weak acids have few H⁺ ions.
mistakes.right: Many or few H⁺ ions, or a high or low concentration of H⁺ ions, is not allowed. Say strong acids are fully ionised and weak acids are partially ionised.

mistakes.wrong: A strong acid is more ionised than a weak acid.
mistakes.right: More ionised is ignored. Say a strong acid is fully ionised or completely dissociated.

mistakes.wrong: The pH increases by 2, so the concentration decreases by a factor of 2.
mistakes.right: Each pH unit is a factor of 10, so two units is 10 × 10 = 100.

worked_example.question:
A scientist measures the pH of some dilute sulfuric acid. The pH is 2.

The scientist makes a solution by adding 990 cm³ of water to 10 cm³ of the dilute sulfuric acid.

Calculate the pH of the solution.
answer_points: The volume has increased by a factor of 1000 ÷ 10 = 100, so the concentration has decreased by a factor of 100.
When the concentration of H⁺ decreases by a factor of 100, the pH increases by 2, so 2 + 2 = pH 4.
worked_example.tip: The answer pH 4 scores all three marks. Show the working in case it is wrong.
